comments.body: i'm working on a monster battling/collecting game like pokemon so for things like battle cries, move sfx and ambient sounds i'm making them myself in a daw, using various samples then processing them.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
I used a wooden painted ball in a metal bowl to make a level up ding. I held my phone sideways and blew across the mic to make rocket afterburner sounds. I smacked a dowel at different angles against my mattress to make punch and kick sounds. I slid scissors against a spoon and slowed it down to make sword sheath noises. For thunder and lightning I just shook a piece of paper and slowed down and sped up the clip, respectively.

I also find noise-dampened rooms make for better sound effects because there is no echo. You can cheat this by being in a dense closet or in a closet with a blanket on the door.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: I usually start with finding sounds on CC0 websites and find a close match to what I want, then Claude can edit the sound a bit. It can also analyze the waveform and attempt to make the sound procedurally which can sound a bit less authentic but takes up way less disk space.
